title: Packaging variants v3 (working draft) — Hosted API bundles + Dedicated add-ons
body:
Context / why v3
- This is a working draft of packaging options for Hosted API (usage-based) + Dedicated capacity add-ons.
- We need clearer “what you get” bundles for self-serve and a consistent story for sales-led, without creating RevRec or billing-dispute risk.
- v3 assumptions: we will bill off “billed_tokens” (not raw tokens) and the usage export will expose billed_tokens and cache attribution (see pr-27485). Any plan that depends on cache discounting MUST be compatible with the meter spec + reconciliation playbook.

Non-negotiables (guardrails)
1) Meter integrity / disputes
- Plans must be implementable strictly from billing ledger + usage events (no manual adjustments to make packaging math work).
- Token definition must be consistent across Redwood native + OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Retries/fallback: only one billable usage record per customer request idempotency key (see ENG/PR work on dedupe).

2) RevRec + audit trail
- Simple mapping from contract line items → meters → invoice line items.
- Credits/discounts should apply to the same base meter used for pricing (billed_tokens), and the application rules must be deterministic.

3) Customer comprehension
- “Included usage + predictable overage” is easier than model-specific complexity for self-serve.
- For enterprise, we can tolerate more structure, but we must avoid ambiguous definitions (cache hits, tool calls, streaming partials).

Key meter definitions (working)
- Billed tokens = prompt_billed_tokens + completion_billed_tokens, derived from the server-side tokenizer used in the meter spec.
- Streaming: billed tokens accrue as generated; if a client disconnects, billed tokens equal tokens successfully generated/streamed (per meter spec).
- Tool/function calling: tool-call tokens are attributed to the completion side for billing purposes (unless spec changes).
- Cache hit attribution: v3 plans treat cache-hit tokens as billable unless explicitly discounted in-plan. (Discounting cache hits is a separate toggle with risk; see Open Questions.)

Pricing primitives (what we can bundle)
A) Included monthly tokens (by input vs output)
- Pro: straightforward and maps cleanly to current meters.
- Con: customers hate thinking about two counters unless we explain it well.

B) Included “Total billed tokens” pooled (input+output combined)
- Pro: simplest customer story.
- Con: cost exposure if output-heavy workloads. Needs careful rate-setting and margin model.

C) Included dollar credits (prepaid spend)
- Pro: operationally easiest for multi-model catalogs; naturally handles model price changes.
- Con: can feel like gift cards; less intuitive for devs who want unit economics per token.

D) “Model tiers” (Standard vs Premium)
- Pro: simplifies margin management.
- Con: adds catalog governance burden + customer confusion when models move tiers.


PACKAGING VARIANT 1 (recommended self-serve baseline): “Included tokens + predictable overage”
Summary: 3 self-serve plans with included usage by input/output tokens, monthly reset, hard caps optional, overage always on by default unless customer disables.

Plan definitions (draft numbers; FP&A to validate vs GM model)
Note: rates are placeholders and assume we keep separate input/output meters.

1) Starter (self-serve)
- Price: $49 / month
- Included: 20M input billed tokens + 10M output billed tokens
- Overage: $0.75 / 1M input + $2.25 / 1M output
- Limits: 60 RPM default, bursts allowed with “trust tier” upgrade; max context length per model default.
- Support: community + best-effort
- Positioning: “Build + ship small features; predictable bill.”
- Feasibility: high (simple monthly included buckets; existing meters)

2) Pro (self-serve / light sales-assist)
- Price: $499 / month
- Included: 250M input + 125M output
- Overage: $0.65 / 1M input + $1.95 / 1M output
- Extras: higher rate limits, longer retention in Console (e.g., 14 days traces), basic SSO optional add-on
- Support: email support, 2 business day response target
- Positioning: “Production workloads without procurement.”
- Feasibility: high

3) Scale (sales-led but can be self-serve upgrade)
- Price: $4,000 / month
- Included: 2.5B input + 1.25B output
- Overage: $0.55 / 1M input + $1.65 / 1M output
- Extras: SLA-lite, priority routing tier, 30 days observability retention, spend alerts + budget controls
- Support: priority support, shared Slack channel (optional)
- Positioning: “Growing usage; lower unit cost; operational controls.”
- Feasibility: medium (SLA/priority routing touches control plane policies; confirm gating)

Overage behavior / billing details
- Overage computed daily but billed monthly with the subscription invoice.
- If customer disables overage: requests over the included amount are rejected with a clear error and a Console banner.
- All overage uses billed_tokens, not raw tokens.

Pros
- Aligns to dev mental model (included usage) and reduces sticker shock via predictable overage.
- Easy to reconcile (included buckets + overage) provided meters are stable.

Cons / risks
- Two counters (input + output) adds cognitive load and sales friction.
- Customers will compare to providers that quote “single blended per-token price.”

Operational feasibility notes (what Eng needs)
- Quota system must support separate monthly buckets for input and output tokens.
- Usage API must show: input_billed_tokens, output_billed_tokens, cache_hit fields, request_count.
- Invoices should match usage exports on the same dimensions (account_id, day, model, region).


PACKAGING VARIANT 2 (simplify customer story): “Pooled billed tokens”
Summary: 1 pooled token bucket per month. All billed tokens count the same regardless of prompt vs completion.

Draft plan definitions
- Starter: $99/mo includes 50M pooled billed tokens; overage $1.25 / 1M
- Pro: $999/mo includes 750M pooled billed tokens; overage $1.05 / 1M
- Scale: $7,500/mo includes 7.5B pooled billed tokens; overage $0.90 / 1M

Pros
- Very simple customer story and easier to estimate.

Cons / risks
- Output-heavy customers become less profitable unless we raise price (risking conversion).
- Engineering cost drivers correlate more strongly with output tokens than input; pooled pricing hides that.

Feasibility
- High for billing (single bucket) but requires careful margin tuning and possibly model gating.


PACKAGING VARIANT 3 (enterprise-friendly + pricing-change-proof): “Prepaid spend credits (RIU)”
Summary: customers buy monthly credits (dollars), and usage subtracts at published list rates per model.

Structure
- Subscription line: “Monthly Inference Credit” (e.g., $10k, $25k, $100k)
- Usage line(s): metered token charges at list; credit applies automatically until exhausted; then overage at list (or contracted) rates.

Pros
- Naturally handles multi-model catalog + future rate changes; simplest for order forms.
- Clean for RevRec: prepaid vs usage recognized per consumption.

Cons
- Less transparent for developers; looks like “prepay.”
- Requires best-in-class usage visibility (customers will demand daily burn-down).

Feasibility
- Medium: we need clear rules for credit application ordering across meters/models/regions.


Dedicated add-ons (applies to Variants 1–3)
Goal: give customers an upgrade path to predictable throughput/latency and data isolation.

Dedicated Add-on A: “Dedicated Pool - Standard”
- Commit: starting at 1 GPU (monthly), customer chooses region + GPU class (limited options)
- Meter: GPU-seconds (per meter v2 definition) with a monthly included commit; burst billed at on-demand rate
- SLA: higher uptime/latency SLO and priority incident response
- Notes: must map cleanly to GPU-seconds v2 and should run shadow compare before billing changes

Dedicated Add-on B: “Dedicated Pool - Burst Pack”
- No fixed commit; customer prepays a burst budget (e.g., 500 GPU-hours) usable within the month
- Intended for launches/spikes
- Risk: creates “credit-like” behavior inside Dedicated; keep as sales-led only unless we can make billing crystal-clear

Dedicated Add-on C: “Private networking + compliance pack” (for Hosted API customers who don’t want full Private)
- Add-on fee: monthly
- Includes: VPC peering / private link option, audit log exports, longer retention, compliance docs
- Requires: access control + audit trail consistency (ties into data retention policy)


Discounting / credits (how packaging interacts)
- Self-serve: credits only for incident remediation; no bespoke discounting.
- Sales-led: allow contracted overage rates and/or committed spend discounts with approval matrix.
- Credits must apply to the same meter used for invoice calculation (billed_tokens or GPU-seconds), and show as a separate line on invoice + in usage export.


Positioning notes (Soojins working copy direction)
- Starter: “Start building. Included usage. Don’t get surprised.”
- Pro: “Production-ready. Higher limits. Better visibility.”
- Scale: “Lower unit cost + controls. SLAs available.”
- Dedicated: “Predictable performance and isolation. Best for regulated or steady throughput.”


Experiment / rollout notes (ties to Q1 experiments)
- We should not run packaging A/B tests that overlap with meter definition changes without explicit pre/post segmentation.
- Variant 1 is the cleanest to experiment with because it least depends on new meters beyond billed_tokens exposure.
- Cohorts: new self-serve signups only; exclude existing customers unless opt-in and contract amendment is clear.


Open questions (need alignment before we finalize)
1) Cache-hit billing
- Do we want to discount cache-hit tokens (e.g., 50% rate) as a packaging feature?
- Pros: strong story (“you benefit from caching”). Cons: hard to explain, increased dispute risk if attribution is wrong.
- If yes, we need: (a) a stable cache_hit attribution field, (b) reconciliation checks for cache hit rate drift, (c) explicit contract language.

2) Retries / fallback
- Confirm policy: server-side retry/fallback should not double bill; client retries with new idempotency key are new requests.
- Need to align SDK guidance and public docs.

3) Token counting parity
- Confirm OpenAI-compatible endpoints show the exact same token breakdown as Redwood native, including tool-call tokens.

4) Overage default
- Default overage ON (preferred for revenue + user experience) vs default OFF (preferred for “no surprises”).
- Possible compromise: overage ON with spend caps + alerts by default.

5) Plan limits
- Which limits are productized (RPM/TPM, concurrency, max context, model allowlist) and which are sales-only?

6) Dedicated pricing unit
- Are we quoting GPU-hours or GPU-seconds externally? Finance prefers invoices in a human unit (hours), but the meter is GPU-seconds. Need consistent display conversion rules and rounding.


Next steps / owners
- FP&A (Rishi): sanity-check draft numbers vs gross margin model with latest meter assumptions.
- Product (Nikhil): pick top 1–2 variants to test; define success metrics + stop criteria with Product Ops.
- Finance/RevRec (Emily): confirm invoice line item structure + credit application rules are audit-safe.
- Telemetry/Eng (Logan/Nadia): confirm feasibility of separate buckets, cache-hit attribution stability, and required usage API fields.
- PMO (Talia): schedule exec review; ensure Legal review of customer-facing “usage definition” copy before any external launch.

Change log
- v3 (2026-02-23): added Dedicated add-ons section; clarified billed_tokens dependency; added cache-hit open question; aligned on “no retro invoice changes without approval.”
- v2 (2026-02-10): first full plan table + overage behavior notes.
